results.description:
Once we know how much water can be stored within the effective rooting zone (our bucket), we need to determine the amount of water that can be depleted before irrigation is required to avoid crop water stress.

Maximum allowable depletion, or MAD, is the fraction of plant available water that can be removed from the soil through evapotranspiration (the evaporation from the soil and leaf surfaces plus the transpiration from the plant) before crop stress (Figure 3). [...] Using the previous example, we determined that pasture/hay grass has a maximum allowable depletion value of 60% (Table 1). We also determined that the soil within the effective root zone can store 2.8 inches of plant-available water.

To determine the maximum allowable depletion for pasture/hay:
